question: Should OpenClaw expose `agents.defaults.compaction.enabled: false` as a supported operator opt-out when it disables proactive embedded auto-compaction but deliberately retains overflow recovery and manual `/compact`?
rationale: The patch cleanly implements its stated limited behavior, but the decision creates a new documented configuration and support contract rather than restoring an established public option.

options.title: Sponsor the scoped opt-out
options.body: Accept the documented limited semantics and merge after the branch is refreshed against current main.

options.title: Defer the setting
options.body: Keep current automatic-compaction policy until maintainers define whether a broader or differently named control is desired.

options.title: Define a broader contract first
options.body: Require an owner-approved design that states which proactive, preflight, and overflow-recovery paths a future setting must govern.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the scoped opt-out
recommendation.body: Accept the documented limited semantics and merge after the branch is refreshed against current main.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties steipete to the relevant agent and configuration surface, including adjacent compaction configuration changes.
